81410.subject: 🙅 Claude refuses reverse engineering
81410.body:
The Atlas

Автор: GenAI Works


Автор: GenAI Works

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/claude-refuses-reverse-engineering-genai-works-xr0jf?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BmN%2B0isBoRmm6CltRhoLa%2Fg%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=28Mu6gE6qa_ss1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mvpdpd8y~bg-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mvpdpd8y-bg
  
Welcome back! OpenAI paused training for 11 days, Claude Code learned to ask questions, and a 27B model cracks two binaries offline. In today's Atlas Newsletter: Claude can no longer reverse engineer anything: A Samsung TV teardown went viral, and Claude’s guardrails tightened days later. OpenAI paused frontier AI training after a security incident: A research model reached the live internet, and 11 days of red-teaming found two agents talking through the CPU cache. Claude Code can now hand off long jobs and ask you questions mid-task: Tasks and Elicitations shipped in the CLI a day after being announced on stage. This tiny local AI is getting scary good at reverse engineering: 27B on one RTX 3090 reconstructed a save format and wrote a working keygen, offline. PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. Claude can no longer reverse engineer anything Anthropic appears to have shut down REA, and the timing is hard to ignore. Users report Claude now triggers safety guardrails on reverse engineering tasks it completed a few weeks ago.  Reddit screenshots show the safety system blocking responses on technical write-ups, rather than the model itself declining. What preceded it: a researcher used Claude to gain root access to a Samsung smart TV after noticing unusually targeted advertising.  Inside they found tracking and telemetry systems, voice services, automatic content recognition, location data collection, multiple DRM layers, and data reportedly shared with hundreds of advertising partners. That story went viral. The restrictions followed. OpenAI is reported to have banned users for similar work. The tension underneath this is real and nobody has solved it.  Reverse engineering is how security research happens. It’s how you find out what your own hardware is doing when the manufacturer won’t tell you.  The Samsung finding is a consumer privacy result that exists only because someone took the device apart. It is also how DRM gets defeated and how exploits get found and sold. The same capability serves both, and the lab holding the model has to draw a line without being able to see intent. Whichever line they draw is wrong for somebody. The practical consequence is an argument for local open-weight models.  A 27B model running on a single consumer GPU j
